Charleston website design has an unusual job. On the peninsula a contractor may need to explain a review board before a homeowner trusts him with an old window or a slate roof. A florist or a planner is competing for couples who live in Ohio and have never seen the venue. A shop on King Street is selling to locals and visitors in the same afternoon. A site built from a generic template answers none of those people well.

Dominion Web Design Pro is one person, Maurice Johnson, who writes every page by hand and shows you a free demo before you spend a dollar. The prices are printed and paid once.

Charleston website design for work a review board will see

The City of Charleston's Board of Architectural Review looks at new construction and exterior alterations in the city's historic districts that can be seen from a public street. In the Old and Historic District, demolitions go to the Board no matter how old the building is. Smaller items such as painting, signs, sitework and repairs are usually approved at staff level, and a staff decision can be appealed to the Board. The Board itself is split in two: one panel for large projects and one for small ones.

For a roofer, a window restorer, a mason or a painter, that process is part of the sale. A homeowner who has heard stories about approvals wants to know whether you will handle the paperwork, how long the review tends to add, and what happens if the first submittal is sent back.

So the site should say it. Not with promises about approvals, which nobody can make, but with a calm explanation of how you work: who prepares the drawings, when you submit, what you need from the owner, and how you keep the job moving while you wait. That one page does more for a peninsula contractor than any slogan.

A page plan for a historic home contractor

PageWhat it tells the homeowner
HomeThe trades you cover, the areas you work in, a phone button and a short line on review-board projects.
Historic workHow you handle exterior work in the historic districts: drawings, submittals, staff review versus Board review, and the effect on your schedule.
ServicesOne section per trade, written in the words owners use: wood windows, slate and tile roofs, stucco, piazza repair.
Service areaThe peninsula, West Ashley, James Island, Mount Pleasant and the other places you really drive to.
About and contactWho shows up on the job, how to reach you, and a form that emails each request straight to you.

That is the Starter package's five pages. Pro adds room for a photo gallery of your own jobs and ten city pages.

Web design Charleston SC wedding vendors can book from

Weddings are a real slice of the local economy. In 2022 Explore Charleston said the area hosts more than 4,100 weddings in a given year and projected about $108 million in direct spending from them that year. Planners, florists, photographers, caterers, rental companies, hair and makeup artists, musicians and venues all chase those couples, and many of the couples are planning from out of state.

A couple planning from far away cannot drop by. They judge you on photos, on how clearly you describe what is included, and on how easy it is to ask whether their date is open. The pages that help them most are simple: what you do, the venues or areas you work, a starting price if you are willing to share one, and an inquiry form that asks for the date, the venue and the guest count so you can answer in one reply.

Vendors also get found through each other. A florist who lists the venues she regularly works with, with permission, gives Google and couples a reason to connect her name with those places.

Charleston SC web design by part of town

The city had about 155,400 residents in the Census Bureau's 2023 estimate, and Charleston County about 436,200 in 2025. Customers rarely search for "Charleston" alone; they search for where they are.

King Street and Upper King

King Street was named one of the American Planning Association's Great Places in America in 2014. Its upper end is often called the Design and Dining District, packed with restaurants, bars and independent shops.

Mount Pleasant

Its own town, on the east side of the Cooper River, linked to the peninsula by the Ravenel Bridge. A Mount Pleasant customer looking for a dentist or a fence builder expects to see Mount Pleasant named on your site if you really serve it.

West Ashley

The part of the city west of the Ashley River. Residents there search with “West Ashley” in the query, so a salon or repair shop there should use the name the way locals do.

James Island and Johns Island

Islands reached by bridges: the Wappoo Bridge links West Ashley to James Island, and Johns Island lies across the Stono River beyond it. A lawn crew or a pool service should say plainly whether it crosses the bridges.

North Charleston

Its own city with its own addresses, and the home of the Charleston Area SBDC and the local SCORE chapter office. A business here should say North Charleston, not just Charleston.

Summerville

About 51,900 people lived inside town limits in the 2023 estimate. Owners there search for web design in Summerville, SC, and their customers search by town name too.

Google says local results weigh relevance, distance and prominence. A house cleaner based in Summerville will not show up for every search in Mount Pleasant, but a truthful page about the Mount Pleasant work she does gives her a fair chance where she really travels.

The Pro package includes ten city pages, each researched and written for one place. Agency starts with keyword research across your whole service area and adds a page for each town and service pair worth having.

Free help in the Lowcountry before you spend

  • Charleston Area SBDCPart of the South Carolina Small Business Development Center network, at 6296 Rivers Avenue in North Charleston. A 2021 report also listed an office at The Citadel, so ask which location is closest to you.
  • SCORE CharlestonVolunteer business mentors who give free, confidential mentoring. The chapter lists an office on Bridge View Drive in North Charleston.
  • Charleston Metro Chamber of CommerceThe regional chamber says about 80% of its members are small businesses, and it keeps a small business resources page for members.

A counselor can help with the plan and the money. When you are ready for the website, that part is what we do.

Common questions

How much do web designers charge for a website in Charleston?

It depends on who builds it and how much is custom. Local agency quotes are often given only after a discovery meeting, and freelancers range widely. Our prices are printed: Starter is $497, Pro is $997 and Agency is $1,997, each paid one time. Hosting, maintenance and updates are $49 a month, or included while you keep the AI agent. You see a demo of your own site before paying anything.

Is there a Charleston web designer who will show me the site before I pay?

That is how we work. Give us your business name and what you do, and Maurice builds a demo for you to look at. If it is not right, you owe nothing. We are not in Charleston, though: every site is written and built remotely from Big Sandy, Texas, and you approve each page before it goes live.

Do you do web design in Summerville, SC?

Yes. Summerville businesses get the same process and prices as anyone on the peninsula. If you serve both Summerville and Charleston, the Pro package includes ten city pages, so Summerville, North Charleston or Mount Pleasant can each get a page written about that place instead of one page with the town name swapped.

Can my contractor website explain the Board of Architectural Review process?

It should, if you work on historic properties. A plain page that says what kinds of exterior work usually need review, that you handle the drawings and submittals, and how the review fits into your schedule answers the first question many peninsula homeowners ask. We write it from what you tell us about your own process, not from guesses.

Can a wedding vendor take inquiries by date through the website?

Yes. Every package includes a contact form that emails each inquiry to you, and we can set the fields you need: event date, venue, guest count and budget range. A full booking engine with live calendars and deposits is custom software and is not part of our packages; we will say so before you buy.

Want to see a Charleston site written for your trade?

Give us your business name and what you do, and a demo site gets built for you to look at on your own phone. If you like it, pick a package. If you do not, you have spent nothing but the minute it took to look.
